newsitem.title: THAILAND: Khmer Rouge hardliners capture dissident village.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge hardliners capture dissident village.

text.p: Hardline Khmer Rouge guerrillas captured a northern Cambodian village held by a dissident rebel faction, the first captured by the Pol Pot loyalists since the group's split, Thai and Cambodian officials said on Thursday.
No information was available on the number of casualties from Wednesday's 20-minute clash, but Thai officials said the fighting sent hundreds of villagers fleeing to Thailand in panic.
"There are some 140 refugees, mostly women and children, under the protection of the Thai army," a Thai army spokesman near the Cambodian border told Reuters.
The village of Joop Kaki had been held by the dissident group which broke from Pol Pot's hardline faction last month.
A Cambodian official said most of the refugees had returned to their jungle village late on Wednesday.
"All Cambodians will soon return to their home because the government is sending troops to help them recapture the village today," Long Sarin of the Cambodian embassy told Reuters.

The breakaway faction, which is negotiating a peace deal with Phnom Penh, is led by Ieng Sary, the foreign minister during the Khmer Rouge's reign of terror under Pol Pot which began in April 1975 and lasted more than three years.
More than one million Cambodians died from execution, starvation or malaria during Khmer Rouge rule.
Sporadic fighting between the dissidents and Pol Pot's faction began shortly after Ieng Sary announced the breakaway and formed a new organisation called the Democratic National United Movement.
The Khmer Rouge guerrillas signed a U.N.-brokered Cambodia peace pact in 1991, but reneged on the accord and have been fighting the coalition that emerged from general elections in 1993.
